driver: A pool of returnable containers circulates between a plant and many holders; the quantity to buy is the busiest week's need less the usable pool, and neither is recorded: the pool's losses are the residual of counts that also carry other owners' containers and own containers coming back by another route, the usable pool is a register that still holds every container lost since its last reconciliation, a holder's stock is one container in use per dispense point plus cover for its delivery interval rather than a share of its throughput, and a plant's full stock of small items made in fixed lots scales with the lot and the number of items rather than with throughput, so a pool-wide turns ratio that back-tests well on the record misplaces every part of the forward need.
driver_concrete: to be filled when the pack is cut
stump: A careful but hurried analyst reconciles the gate counters for the loss (foreign kegs in the empties and own kegs returned through the exchange hide most of it), takes the register as the usable fleet (it still holds every keg lost since the November 2023 reconciliation), carries 2026's keg turns to the Maplestead estate's lines (each holds one keg on tap and a week's cover whatever it sells) and to the Foundry range's 18 small-batch beers (each brew fills its whole lot at once), and lands a different wrong order on each size
deep_chain: (1) the year's own-keg loss by size: depot fulls out against own kegs back by every route (the depots' empties less the foreign kegs the washer rejects, the exchange's and the recovery agent's returns), less the rise in kegs in the trade; (2) the usable fleet: on-site stocktake plus kegs in the trade (tagged kegs' states scaled, the recent trips completed from settled ones, the seasonal holders' winter stock kept) plus the exchange's balance, against the register less its untraced kegs; (3) the busiest week's fills at normal weather with its range across ten summers; (4) the estate's kegs from a holding model per line fitted on the outlets' own stocks; (5) the Foundry range's full stock walked week by week from the 2027 brew plan; (6) the need in circulation at the busiest week by component; (7) the order
judgment: a loss residual whose counts carry other owners' kegs and miss own kegs returned by another route; a usable fleet no record holds; a holding per dispense line that does not scale with throughput; a lot-size full stock that does not scale with throughput
one_fact_test: to be computed: the strongest sentence (a pub holds one keg on tap and its delivery cover on every line whatever it sells) rescues the estate's kegs and part of the need, not the loss, the fleet, the forecast or the Foundry stock

lineage.driver: A forward workload is forecast through a per-unit rate that rises once more workers share a fixed space, a rise the coarse record hides because the busy periods carry lighter units, so a proportional scaling its own back-test confirms plans the busy periods short; the forward volume comes from a forecaster whose overstatement grows with the growth it plans and whose period profile is keyed to a calendar grid that a long year moves a whole step against the events driving demand, and a new stream's per-unit work is measured on a pilot whose units were drawn from its lightest class, so which periods need a second shift and how many extra hours to book come out only when every correction is carried together.
lineage.driver_concrete: Saarnela's 2027 peak plan forecasts each small-parts zone's paid picker hours from Kotikaari Oy's year-ahead weekly forecast, which overstates by a share that grows with the growth it plans and copies 2025's week numbers into a calendar shifted a week by 2026's 53 ISO weeks (Black Friday falls in week 47 of 2027), through a time per line by handling class and units with an aisle-congestion term that the peak's lighter lines hide in the weekly record, and with Huippu Sport's lines at its full peak assortment (footwear boxes, multi-unit lines) where the September pilot stocked only polybag apparel; the day shift's capacity at each zone's limit of pickers on the floor decides the evening-shift weeks and the remainder sets the agency booking; on the cut pack the golden opens the evening shift in weeks 47 to 50 in both zones (week 46 at 0.84 and 0.87 of the day shifts' capacity, weeks 47 to 50 at 1.17 to 1.30), the draft's route in week 48 only.
lineage.stump: The careful pass measures the pooled overstatement (right) and applies it to every week of the client's 2027 forecast, keeping the forecast's week-numbered profile (Black Friday a week late) and pricing its planned growth at the pooled rate; it fits time per line on the handling-class mix at the weekly or shift grain, where the peak's lighter lines hide the aisle congestion, so the 2025 peak's rate carries to 2027's denser floor and the draft's back-test confirms it; and it reads Huippu Sport's time per line off the pilot, whose polybag assortment picks quicker than Kotikaari's lines: it books too few agency hours in the busiest weeks and opens the evening shift in the wrong weeks.

lineage.driver: Each unit's forward demand is the sum of event streams that follow different exposures, and the record's exposures moved together, so every in-sample check passes on the conventional one while the forward plan decouples them; part of the stream is repeated swaps driven by a fault in the host rather than the item, so the items flagged by their own counts are mostly the host's victims or chance and regress; a fix converts the population item by item at each item's own visit; every line's turnaround runs through one shared queue that lengthens nonlinearly as the forward load rises; and demand clusters in shared shocks, so the stock each line needs is set by the clustered, queue-lengthened pipeline, never by its average.
